text:
Lucita, what sorrow

it gives me to see, wrapped in timid flashes

of moon, your fields,

your dark earth;

the hill that rises

with the capulín trees for which you sighed,

and those roads along which you passed

bathed and barefoot!

What sad sorrow!

Your field is in shadows, for you were the light;

and in the cemetery, after you left,

they have put another cross...

One day they said you were lost,

and thorns wounded your own old mother;

and when summer stripped the orchards bare

they found your dear mother asleep,

but with her eyes

open...

You did not understand that the city was

fire that consumes with its wicked lights,

and that it burns the wings

of innocence from little Lucitas...

translation.title: Over There...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the rural lament for Lucita and the city as destructive fire.
